source_caption:
One of the greatest lies in prestige television is “I did it for my family.” In Breaking Bad, The Sopranos, and Succession, that line becomes a mask for ego, power, control, and self-justification — because the tragedy isn’t that these men don’t love their families, it’s that they use love as the excuse for everything they destroy.

Breaking Bad, The Sopranos & Succession, created by Vince Gilligan, David Chase, and Jesse Armstrong, starring Bryan Cranston, James Gandolfini, Brian Cox. Three defining television dramas about men who claim to protect their families while slowly revealing that legacy, dominance, and pride may have been the real addiction all along.

source_details.title: Succession
source_details.synopsis: Succession is an American satirical comedy-drama television series created by English screenwriter Jesse Armstrong that aired for four seasons on HBO from June 3, 2018, to May 28, 2023. The series centers on the Roy family, the owners of global media and entertainment conglomerate Waystar RoyCo, and their fight for control of the company amidst uncertainty about the health of the family's patriarch. Brian Cox portrays the family patriarch Logan Roy. His children are played by Alan Ruck as Connor, Jeremy Strong as Kendall, Kieran Culkin as Roman, and Sarah Snook as Shiv.
